text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Demand for young employees has clearly increased and it is not impossible to find a summer job, an informal survey by the newspaper of the labour market shows.
- Strong British pound has not scared off Swedish tourists to the country.

- The finance inspectorate has filed a claim with authorities about alledged insider trading in connection with investment group Incentive's take over of medical technology group Gambro. Incentive's bid price for Gambro represented a 30 percent premium on the market price.
- No details of finance inspectorate complaint on insider trading in connection with Incentive's bid for Gambro are available.

- Support for Swedish membership in Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) has risen with 30 percent of Swedes now saying they are in support of the project compared to about 25 percent at an earlier poll in March 1996.
- Futures and options exchange OM Group posted a record high pre-tax H1 profit of 209 million crowns, up from 164 million crowns in the year-ago period.

- Swedish ten-year bond yield fell over 10 basis points in a week to 6.42 percent -- the lowest level in several decades. Several economists say this is the bottom but an upturn is expected to be moderate.
